title: Job 4
paragraphs: ¹ Then Eliphaz the Temanite replied: ² "If someone tries to speak with you, will you be impatient? But who can keep from speaking? ³ Think of how you have instructed many and have strengthened feeble hands. ⁴ Your words have steadied those who were falling, and you have strengthened trembling knees. ⁵ But now trouble has come to you, and you are overwhelmed; it strikes you, and you fall apart.

⁶ "Should not your reverence for God give you confidence? Should not your blameless ways be your hope? ⁷ Think carefully — has the innocent ever perished? Has the upright ever been destroyed? ⁸ What I have seen is this: those who plow evil and sow trouble reap the same. ⁹ They perish by the breath of God; they are consumed by the blast of his anger. ¹⁰ The roar of the lion, the growl of the great lion — even the teeth of the young lions are broken.

¹¹ The mighty lion perishes for lack of prey, and the cubs of the lioness scatter. ¹² Now a word was secretly brought to me; my ear caught a whisper of it. ¹³ It came to me in disturbing visions of the night, when deep sleep falls on people. ¹⁴ Fear and trembling seized me and made all my bones shake. ¹⁵ A spirit glided past my face, and the hair on my body stood on end.

¹⁶ It stopped, but I could not make out its form; a shape was before my eyes, and I heard a hushed voice: ¹⁷ 'Can a mortal be more righteous than God? Can even a strong man be more pure than his Maker? ¹⁸ If God places no trust in his servants, if he charges his angels with error, ¹⁹ how much more those who live in houses of clay, whose foundations are in the dust, who are crushed more easily than a moth! ²⁰ Between dawn and dusk they are shattered; unnoticed, they perish forever.
²¹ Are not the tent cords of their life pulled up? They die without ever gaining wisdom.'
